kubernetes-cks-s1.1-05.reason: weak_card: strawman (port 443 validating TLS); verifier replacement confirmed on concepts page list of what NetworkPolicy cannot do (final: keep)
kubernetes-cks-s1.1-05.statement: The NetworkPolicy API lets a policy author request logging of the connections a policy blocks.
kubernetes-cks-s1.1-05.explanation: NetworkPolicy has no field for logging blocked or accepted connections; any such visibility comes from network plugin features or other tooling.
kubernetes-cks-s1.1-05.misconception: NetworkPolicy can ask the dataplane to log the connections it blocks.

kubernetes-cks-s1.1-10.reason: tell: removes proof verb 'confirms' from a false statement; fact and answer unchanged (final: fixed)
kubernetes-cks-s1.1-10.statement: The API server waits until the network plugin enforces a new NetworkPolicy before it accepts the object.
kubernetes-cks-s1.1-10.explanation: The API server stores a valid NetworkPolicy without waiting for the network plugin; the Kubernetes API exposes no enforcement-readiness signal, and plugin processing can lag behind.
kubernetes-cks-s1.1-10.misconception: API acceptance confirms installed network enforcement.

kubernetes-cks-s1.2-04.explanation: kube-bench detects which components run on its host and selects tests from that, so control-plane file checks need the Job scheduled on a control-plane node.

kubernetes-cks-s1.2-07.reason: weak_card: vague, near-true by wording; verifier replacement confirmed on the Ingress page TLS note (final: keep)

kubernetes-cks-s1.2-07.explanation: TLS does not work on the hostless default rule, because its certificate would have to cover every possible hostname; hosts in the tls section must explicitly match rule hosts.

kubernetes-cks-s1.3-02.misconception: A config-file kubelet opens the unauthenticated read-only port unless an administrator disables it.
